name: agent-page
description: Show the operator a live web page in the tclaude dashboard via `tclaude agent show <target>` (short for `tclaude agent page show`), and list or close your pages with `tclaude agent page ls|close`. When the operator draws on a page and sends it (`[page <name>] marks` in your inbox), read the marks with `page marks`, render the page with them with `page snapshot`, and read its DOM with `page dom`. Try a change live, without a source change, with `page css`, `page dom --set-*` and `page eval`; manage those with `page patches`. The target is your own dev server (`:5173/path` or `http://localhost:5173/path`) or a static directory or HTML file in the directory you were started in. The operator sees it live and interactive in a sandboxed frame. Use when you want the operator to look at a UI you are building (instead of rendering a mock to a PNG), or when they ask to "show me", "let me see it", or "put it in the dashboard". Needs `self.page` (default-granted).

findings.excerpt: tclaude agent page marks landing --since 0     # each mark, and the elements under it
tclaude agent page snapshot landing --watch --for 30s -o /tmp/landing.png   # as a background run
tclaude agent page css landing 'button.pay { background: #1971c2 }'
